what_happened: After the 4.6 s handoff, the ego braked hard on the open highway (17 → 8 m/s) with no slower lead ahead. At the same time it planned and steered left toward the next lane, so its front-left struck actor 1, which was passing on the left. The recorded human trajectory stayed in the lane and kept speed. The hard braking likely also explains the separate rear contact.

After handoff on a straight highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (17 to 8 m/s, lead 20+ m away and pulling away). At the same time it drifted left off its lane and the recorded path, and its front hit actor 1 in the adjacent left lane. The ego was also rear-ended at some point, probably because of the sudden braking.

After handoff the policy's plan drifted left out of the ego's lane, against the STRAIGHT and then RIGHT command and away from the recorded path, which went slightly right. The ego moved into the left lane just as pickup 41 was passing on that side and hit it with its front.

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT route command, the policy braked hard (26.5 to 13.2 m/s) and steered left, away from the recorded path that moves right. By 8.1 s it had drifted past the left edge of the leftmost lane toward the median guardrail and went off-road. The rear contact was already in the run's totals and the smeared car in the last frame appears only at the failure moment, so neither explains the drift.

The road curved left (the command changed to LEFT), but the policy kept its plan straight along the right edge of the rightmost lane. The ego went over the right road boundary onto the shoulder at about 13 m/s, 2.6 m off the human path. The camera view was clean, so nothing in the rendering explains the mistake.

On the highway, after the handoff the ego slowed sharply (17 to 8 m/s) and steered left toward the adjacent lane, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in its lane or went right. Actor 1 was overtaking in that left lane, and the ego's front corner hit its side.

As the road curved left (the command changed to LEFT), the ego kept heading straight and slowly drifted right onto the shoulder and paved area beside the road, ending about 2.7 m off the human's path. No other actors were involved, and the camera view was clean until the end.

After handoff, the ego braked hard on the highway (28.8 to 13.4 m/s), and a following vehicle hit its rear. Instead of following the RIGHT command and the recorded path to the right, it drifted left across its lane onto the left shoulder by the median barrier and went offroad 5 m from the recorded trajectory, with a vehicle merging just ahead of it.

The command was STRAIGHT, then RIGHT, and the route (green) held its lane, but the policy's planned path (orange) kept bending left. At about 4.3 m/s the ego drifted into the lane on its left and its front hit actor 41, a pickup driving alongside in that lane, which is clearly visible in the camera at impact.

The road bends left (the command changes from STRAIGHT to LEFT) and the recorded path follows the curve. The ego kept driving almost straight in the rightmost lane, slowing only slightly (about 16 to 13 m/s), and went off the right edge onto the shoulder or sidewalk, about 2.6 m off the recorded path.

After handoff the ego braked hard (29.4 to 12.7 m/s) for no visible reason and steered left, against the RIGHT route command and away from the recorded path. By 7.7s it had crossed the left edge line onto the shoulder (about 5 m off the recorded path), as replayed traffic (actor 40) closed in alongside; the earlier rear contact is likely from the unexplained braking.
